Options and environment variables used by isoformic

Source: R/isoformic-options.R
isoformic-options.Rd

isoformic has five package options, isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit, isoformic.duckdb_threads, isoformic.frozen_mirrors, isoformic.orf_cache and isoformic.workers, and is otherwise configured through base R options, the environment variables that locate the user cache and the settings of the packages it builds on. This page lists every setting the package reads or is affected by, what it changes and where it is used. Settings are read at call time, so they can be changed with options() / Sys.setenv() in a session, scoped with withr::with_options() / withr::with_envvar(), or placed in .Rprofile / .Renviron.

Package options

isoformic.duckdb_threads

Number of threads of the DuckDB connections that read and write Parquet and run the annotation and uncertainty queries: a single positive whole number, such as 4. Default: unset. When SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK is set or the affinity mask of the R process excludes some CPUs (taskset, schedulers that pin cores), isoformic uses the smallest of SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK, the CPUs of the mask and the cgroup CPU quota. Otherwise DuckDB uses all the CPUs of the machine, or the cgroup CPU quota when there is one.

isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit

Memory limit of each DuckDB connection: a single string with a size and a unit, such as "8GB" or "512MiB" (units KB, MB, GB, TB, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB), of at least 1 MiB. A query above it spills to disk when it can and fails otherwise. Default: unset. isoformic then sets 80% of SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE, or of SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU times SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK (or 1), when one is set, or 80% of the cgroup memory limit when that is smaller, and at least 64 MiB; otherwise DuckDB uses 80% of the RAM, or of the cgroup memory limit when there is one. Set it explicitly under ulimit -v, which DuckDB does not see. Both DuckDB options are read when a connection opens a database. A database file that is already open in the session (by a connection that is still open) is shared and keeps the settings it was opened with.

isoformic.frozen_mirrors

Character vector of base URLs tried first by fetch_frozen_data() (and every function that loads a frozen dataset, such as add_appris() or polya_sites(polya_atlas = "polyasite")) before the frozen-data GitHub release and the Zenodo record returned by frozen_mirrors(). Each URL is joined with the file name of the dataset, for example options(isoformic.frozen_mirrors = "https://zenodo.org/records/<id>/files/") pins an analysis to one Zenodo deposit, and "file:///data/isoformic-frozen/" serves the files from a local or institutional mirror. The MD5 recorded in frozen_datasets() is verified whatever the mirror. Default: unset (no extra mirror).

isoformic.orf_cache

FALSE stops transcript_orfs() from reading and writing annot_data_orfs.parquet, the table of the ORFs computed so far that it keeps in the annotation directory. The ORFs are then computed in every session. Default: unset (TRUE).

isoformic.workers

Default of the workers argument of run_enrichment(), run_productivity_enrichment() and run_apa_enrichment(): the number of mirai daemons that run their fgsea calls in parallel, a whole number of at least 1, or "auto" for parallelly::availableCores(). The count is capped at the number of fgsea calls. Default: unset (1, serial, the results of earlier versions). Above 1 every fgsea call gets its own seed, so the sampled p-values differ slightly from a serial run but not between worker counts; see Workers in run_enrichment().

Base R options

timeout

Timeout in seconds of utils::download.file() and url() connections. download_reference(), download_reference_url(), download_hprc_annotation(), download_fantom_cat_tables(), fetch_frozen_data() and the builders in build_frozen_data raise it, for the duration of the download only, to at least the timeout_limit of the call (3600 seconds by default, large reference files are several gigabytes) and never lower it. Set a larger value for slow connections.

download.file.method, download.file.extra

Define what the method = "auto" default of the download functions resolves to and the extra command line flags of the "wget" and "curl" methods. Pass method explicitly to override them for one call.

rlang_interactive

Overrides interactive() for rlang::is_interactive(). In a non-interactive session the download progress is silenced (quiet = TRUE in utils::download.file()) and missing optional packages (for example fgsea, condathis, readxl, Matrix, SummarizedExperiment, or edgeR, limma, satuRn, DEXSeq and BiocParallel for test_usage(), mirai for workers above 1 in the enrichment functions) raise an error instead of an installation prompt.

cli.num_colors, cli.unicode, cli.default_handler, cli.width, cli.progress_show_after, crayon.enabled, crayon.colors

Rendering of every message, warning and error, which the package emits through the cli package (cli also honours the older crayon.* options). cli.unicode = FALSE and cli.num_colors = 1 produce plain ASCII output for logs; crayon.enabled = FALSE turns off ANSI colours, and just test and just test-full set it together with cli.unicode = FALSE; see ?cli::cli-config.

Environment variables

R_USER_CACHE_DIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME

Root of the user cache. get_isoformic_cache() resolves tools::R_user_dir("isoformic", "cache"), which honours R_USER_CACHE_DIR first, then XDG_CACHE_HOME (~/.cache by default on Linux). On macOS the package sets XDG_CACHE_HOME to ~/.cache for the lookup when it is unset, so the cache lives in ~/.cache/R/isoformic/ instead of ~/Library/Caches/org.R-project.R/R/isoformic/ and never contains a space. The cache holds downloaded references (download_reference()), the frozen datasets (frozen/), their sources (sources/<name>/) and the Zenodo bundle (zenodo_deposit/). Point it to a shared or scratch disk on HPC systems.

LOCALAPPDATA

On Windows, the root that tools::R_user_dir() uses when R_USER_CACHE_DIR is unset.

HOME, USERPROFILE

Define the ~ that the defaults above and fs::path_home() expand to.

http_proxy, https_proxy, ftp_proxy, no_proxy

Proxy settings honoured by utils::download.file() and url() (libcurl and internal methods) and therefore by every download in the package, including the connectivity check curl::has_internet() that the download functions run first when curl is installed.

CURL_CA_BUNDLE, SSL_CERT_FILE

Certificate bundle used by the libcurl download method, needed behind TLS-intercepting proxies.

SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK, SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE, SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU

Set by Slurm inside a job. When the isoformic.duckdb_threads and isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit options are unset, they bound the threads and set the memory limit of the DuckDB connections (memory in megabytes, as Slurm writes it; 0 is ignored), so that DuckDB sizes itself to the job and not to the node.

OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS, R_DATATABLE_NUM_THREADS, R_LIBS

Set, for the daemons only, when the enrichment functions start mirai daemons (workers above 1, or isoformic_workers()): the thread variables to 1, so that each daemon uses one core, and R_LIBS to the session's .libPaths(), so that the daemons find the packages of the session. The session's own values are not changed.

Settings of other packages

DuckDB

Every Parquet read and write (read_parquet(), write_parquet(), read_tabular()) and the heavy joins run in a short-lived in-memory DuckDB connection, which is not shared with user code. Its threads and memory_limit come from the isoformic.duckdb_threads and isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit options or the Slurm and affinity defaults described above, and otherwise from DuckDB. Besides these and the storage locations below, the package only turns off the DuckDB progress bar (enable_progress_bar). Extensions, secrets and the files of a query that spills to disk go to isoformic-duckdb/ under tempdir(), unless the duckdb.home option or the DUCKDB_R_HOME environment variable is set: DuckDB then uses its own locations under that directory.

BiocParallel

Each fgsea call of the enrichment functions runs with BiocParallel::SerialParam() unless BPPARAM or nproc is passed through ..., so a backend set with BiocParallel::register() is not used; the calls run in parallel through workers instead. The workers argument of test_usage() is different: it builds a BiocParallel::MulticoreParam() on Unix-like systems.

mirai

With workers above 1 the enrichment functions run on the daemons of the mirai compute profile "isoformic". When that profile has no daemons, they start them (with one thread each) and keep them for the session, resizing them to the workers of later calls and replacing those that died; isoformic_workers() starts a fixed number ahead or stops them, and they are stopped when the session ends or isoformic is unloaded. Daemons that the user started on the profile (mirai::daemons(n, .compute = "isoformic")) are used as they are and left running; each call puts the session's library paths first on the daemon while it runs, but they keep their own thread settings. Starting daemons with mirai::daemons() draws from the session's random number stream (isoformic's own start does not). Needs mirai 2.3.0 or later. Daemons of other profiles, including the default one, are not used or changed.

parallelly

workers = "auto" (or the isoformic.workers option) calls parallelly::availableCores(), which reads the mc.cores option, the MC_CORES, SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK and other scheduler environment variables, the CPU affinity mask and the cgroup CPU quota, and its own parallelly.availableCores.* options and R_PARALLELLY_* variables (see ?parallelly::availableCores). Without parallelly, "auto" is one worker.

condathis.micromamba_path, CONDATHIS_MICROMAMBA_PATH, CONDA_PREFIX, R_USER_DATA_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME

Read by the condathis package, which salmon_index(), salmon_quant() and run_terminus() use to run salmon and Terminus in micromamba environments: where the micromamba binary is found and where environments are created. See ?condathis::condathis.

BIOCONDUCTOR_*, R_LIBS*

Only relevant for installing the optional packages (fgsea, SummarizedExperiment, edgeR, ...); the package itself does not read them.

Development and test settings

These are not read by the package code but control its test suite and checks (see justfile):

ISOFORMIC_FULL

"true" runs the tests and articles that download references or run external tools (just test-full, just render-articles-full, just benchmark-memory). Unset by default: the tests, examples and site then use only the data bundled with the package.

TESTTHAT_CPUS

Number of parallel testthat workers used by just test; it only matters when parallel mode is on.

TESTTHAT_PARALLEL

"true" or "false"; overrides Config/testthat/parallel: true in DESCRIPTION. TESTTHAT_PARALLEL=false runs the test files serially in one process.

NOT_CRAN

Set to "true" by devtools::test(); tests that need optional packages use testthat::skip_if_not_installed(), and only the tests gated by ISOFORMIC_FULL download data.

_R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_

Set to "0" by just check to skip the clock check of R CMD check --as-cran.

HOME, USERPROFILE, R_USER_CACHE_DIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME, R_USER_DATA_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, LOCALAPPDATA, APPDATA

The test setup redirects all of them to temporary directories so that tests never touch the user cache.

warnPartialMatchArgs, warnPartialMatchAttr, warnPartialMatchDollar

Set to TRUE by the test setup, so that a partial match of an argument, attribute or $ name is a warning.

See also

get_isoformic_cache(), frozen_data, download_reference()

Examples

# Pin the frozen datasets to one Zenodo deposit for a reproducible run
withr::with_options(
  list(isoformic.frozen_mirrors = "https://zenodo.org/records/1234567/files/"),
  frozen_mirrors()
)
#> [1] "https://zenodo.org/records/1234567/files/"                          
#> [2] "https://github.com/luciorq/isoformic/releases/download/frozen-data/"

# Where the cache is, and how to move it
get_isoformic_cache()
#> /home/runner/.cache/R/isoformic
withr::with_envvar(
  list(R_USER_CACHE_DIR = tempdir()),
  get_isoformic_cache("frozen")
)
#> /tmp/RtmpPCTCTT/R/isoformic/frozen
